# Clausery

> Clausery is browser-based document automation. It turns ordinary Word (.docx) templates with {tags} into guided questionnaires and generates finished documents entirely on the user's device: no upload, no account, works offline. Free for up to three templates with unlimited documents; the Pro plan adds unlimited templates, calculations, an encrypted workspace and client intake forms.

Key facts:
- Documents are assembled in the browser; template files, answers and generated documents are never sent to a server.
- Templates are normal Word files. Tags: {name} for a value, {#condition}...{/condition} for optional text, {^condition}...{/condition} for the opposite, and {#list}...{/list} for repeating paragraphs or table rows.
- Pro plan: optional passphrase encryption of everything stored in the browser (AES-256-GCM) with auto-lock.
- Free Word templates, a contract clause library and free drafting tools are available without sign-up.
- Clausery is software, not a law firm, and does not give legal advice.

## Product
- [Home](https://bodyatlas.github.io/clausery/): what Clausery does and who it is for
- [Open the app](https://bodyatlas.github.io/clausery/app/): runs in the browser, no sign-up
- [Pricing](https://bodyatlas.github.io/clausery/pricing/): Free, Pro, Team and Enterprise plans

- [Documentation](https://bodyatlas.github.io/clausery/docs/): getting started, template syntax, logic, client intake

## Contract clause library
- [Indemnification clause: meaning and sample wording](https://bodyatlas.github.io/clausery/clauses/indemnification-clause.html): An indemnity is a promise by one party to cover the other party's losses if a specified kind of claim arises, most often a claim by a third party caused by the first party's breach, negligence or infringement of someone else's intellectual property. Free sample indemnification clause wording, what t
- [Limitation of liability clause: meaning and sample wording](https://bodyatlas.github.io/clausery/clauses/limitation-of-liability-clause.html): A limitation of liability clause caps how much one party can recover from the other, and usually excludes whole categories of loss, such as lost profits and indirect or consequential damages. Free sample limitation of liability clause wording, what to check, and FAQs.
- [Force majeure clause: meaning and sample wording](https://bodyatlas.github.io/clausery/clauses/force-majeure-clause.html): A force majeure clause excuses a party from performing, for as long as an extraordinary event outside its control prevents it: natural disasters, war, epidemics, government orders and similar events. Free sample force majeure clause wording, what to check, and FAQs.
- [Confidentiality clause: meaning and sample wording](https://bodyatlas.github.io/clausery/clauses/confidentiality-clause.html): A confidentiality clause obliges a party to keep the other party's non-public information secret, use it only for the purpose of the contract, and share it only with people who need to know it. Free sample confidentiality clause wording, what to check, and FAQs.
- [Non-solicitation clause: meaning and sample wording](https://bodyatlas.github.io/clausery/clauses/non-solicitation-clause.html): A non-solicitation clause stops a party from actively approaching the other party's employees, contractors or customers for a period, usually during the contract and for a time after it ends. Free sample non-solicitation clause wording, what to check, and FAQs.
- [Non-compete clause: meaning and sample wording](https://bodyatlas.github.io/clausery/clauses/non-compete-clause.html): A non-compete clause prevents a person or business from working for, or running, a competing business for a period and within an area after a relationship ends. Free sample non-compete clause wording, what to check, and FAQs.
- [Payment terms clause: meaning and sample wording](https://bodyatlas.github.io/clausery/clauses/payment-terms-clause.html): The payment terms clause says when a party can invoice, how long the other party has to pay, in what currency and by what method, and what happens when an invoice is disputed. Free sample payment terms clause wording, what to check, and FAQs.
- [Late payment interest clause: meaning and sample wording](https://bodyatlas.github.io/clausery/clauses/late-payment-interest-clause.html): A late payment clause lets the party that is owed money charge interest on overdue amounts, and often suspend work until it is paid. Free sample late payment interest clause wording, what to check, and FAQs.
- [Intellectual property assignment clause: meaning and sample wording](https://bodyatlas.github.io/clausery/clauses/intellectual-property-clause.html): An intellectual property clause decides who owns the copyright, designs, inventions and other rights in the work created under a contract, and what each side may do with the other's pre-existing material. Free sample intellectual property assignment clause wording, what to check, and FAQs.
- [Warranty clause: meaning and sample wording](https://bodyatlas.github.io/clausery/clauses/warranty-clause.html): A warranty is a contractual promise about a fact or about quality, such as that services will be performed with reasonable skill and care, or that software will work as specified for 90 days. Free sample warranty clause wording, what to check, and FAQs.
- [Independent contractor clause: meaning and sample wording](https://bodyatlas.github.io/clausery/clauses/independent-contractor-clause.html): This clause records that a person is engaged as an independent business, not as an employee, and that they are responsible for their own taxes, insurance and working arrangements. Free sample independent contractor clause wording, what to check, and FAQs.
- [Termination for convenience clause: meaning and sample wording](https://bodyatlas.github.io/clausery/clauses/termination-for-convenience-clause.html): A termination for convenience clause lets a party end the contract without giving any reason, usually on a period of written notice. Free sample termination for convenience clause wording, what to check, and FAQs.
- [Termination for cause clause: meaning and sample wording](https://bodyatlas.github.io/clausery/clauses/termination-for-cause-clause.html): A termination for cause clause lets a party end the contract when the other party commits a material breach and does not fix it in time, or becomes insolvent. Free sample termination for cause clause wording, what to check, and FAQs.
- [Survival clause: meaning and sample wording](https://bodyatlas.github.io/clausery/clauses/survival-clause.html): A survival clause lists the obligations that continue after a contract ends, such as confidentiality, payment, indemnities and limits on liability. Free sample survival clause wording, what to check, and FAQs.
- [Governing law and jurisdiction clause: meaning and sample wording](https://bodyatlas.github.io/clausery/clauses/governing-law-clause.html): A governing law clause chooses which country's or state's law applies to the contract. Free sample governing law and jurisdiction clause wording, what to check, and FAQs.
- [Dispute resolution clause: meaning and sample wording](https://bodyatlas.github.io/clausery/clauses/dispute-resolution-clause.html): A dispute resolution clause sets out the steps the parties must take when they disagree: usually negotiation between senior people first, then mediation, then arbitration or court. Free sample dispute resolution clause wording, what to check, and FAQs.
- [Notices clause: meaning and sample wording](https://bodyatlas.github.io/clausery/clauses/notices-clause.html): A notices clause says how formal notices under the contract, such as notices of breach, renewal or termination, must be sent, to which address, and when they count as received. Free sample notices clause wording, what to check, and FAQs.
- [Entire agreement clause: meaning and sample wording](https://bodyatlas.github.io/clausery/clauses/entire-agreement-clause.html): An entire agreement clause, also called an integration or merger clause, says that the written contract contains everything the parties agreed, replacing earlier emails, proposals and conversations. Free sample entire agreement clause wording, what to check, and FAQs.
- [Severability clause: meaning and sample wording](https://bodyatlas.github.io/clausery/clauses/severability-clause.html): A severability clause says that if one part of the contract is invalid or unenforceable, the rest of the contract still stands, and the invalid part is trimmed or removed. Free sample severability clause wording, what to check, and FAQs.
- [Assignment clause: meaning and sample wording](https://bodyatlas.github.io/clausery/clauses/assignment-clause.html): An assignment clause says whether a party can transfer its rights under the contract to someone else, for example when it sells its business, and on what conditions. Free sample assignment clause wording, what to check, and FAQs.
- [Amendment clause: meaning and sample wording](https://bodyatlas.github.io/clausery/clauses/amendment-clause.html): An amendment or variation clause says how the contract can be changed, usually only by a written document signed by both parties. Free sample amendment clause wording, what to check, and FAQs.
- [Waiver clause: meaning and sample wording](https://bodyatlas.github.io/clausery/clauses/waiver-clause.html): A no-waiver clause says that if a party does not enforce a right straight away, for example by accepting a late payment without complaint, it has not given that right up. Free sample waiver clause wording, what to check, and FAQs.
- [Counterparts and electronic signature clause: meaning and sample wording](https://bodyatlas.github.io/clausery/clauses/electronic-signature-clause.html): A counterparts clause lets each party sign a separate copy of the contract, with all copies together forming one agreement. Free sample counterparts and electronic signature clause wording, what to check, and FAQs.
- [At-will employment clause: meaning and sample wording](https://bodyatlas.github.io/clausery/clauses/at-will-employment-clause.html): An at-will clause states that either the employer or the employee can end the employment at any time, with or without cause or notice, as US law generally allows. Free sample at-will employment clause wording, what to check, and FAQs.

## Guides
- [How to automate a Word template without uploading it anywhere](https://bodyatlas.github.io/clausery/guides/automate-word-templates.html): A step-by-step guide to turning any Word document into a reusable, fill-in-the-blanks template with questions, conditional clauses and lists, entirely in your browser.
- [Conditional clauses in Word: include or remove paragraphs automatically](https://bodyatlas.github.io/clausery/guides/conditional-clauses-in-word.html): How to make parts of a Word document appear only when they apply: yes/no sections, either/or wording, clauses based on amounts or dates, and removing empty lines.
- [Client intake without a portal: collect answers by email, privately](https://bodyatlas.github.io/clausery/guides/client-intake-without-a-portal.html): How to send clients a questionnaire they can fill in offline and return as a file, so you can generate documents from their answers without a client portal or account.
- [Mail merge vs document automation: which one do you need?](https://bodyatlas.github.io/clausery/guides/mail-merge-vs-document-automation.html): Mail merge fills the same blanks from a spreadsheet; document automation also includes or removes clauses, repeats lists and calculates. How to tell which one your documents need.
- [Repeating lists and table rows in Word templates](https://bodyatlas.github.io/clausery/guides/repeating-lists-and-tables-in-word.html): How to make a Word template repeat a paragraph, bullet or table row for every party, attorney, deliverable or line item, with separators and numbering.
- [Choosing document software when client confidentiality matters: a checklist](https://bodyatlas.github.io/clausery/guides/confidentiality-checklist-document-software.html): Questions to ask before putting client or employee information into any document or drafting tool: where data is processed, who can access it, sub-processors, retention and exit.
- [How to write a job offer letter (with a free template)](https://bodyatlas.github.io/clausery/guides/how-to-write-an-offer-letter.html): What to put in a job offer letter: role, start date, pay, bonus, equity, benefits, conditions and at-will wording, plus the mistakes that cause disputes later.
- [How to write a demand letter for unpaid invoices](https://bodyatlas.github.io/clausery/guides/how-to-write-a-payment-demand-letter.html): A step-by-step guide to asking a customer for overdue payment in writing: what to include, tone, deadlines, interest, and what to do if they still do not pay.
- [What to include in a statement of work (SOW)](https://bodyatlas.github.io/clausery/guides/what-to-include-in-a-statement-of-work.html): The sections every statement of work needs: scope, deliverables, timeline, fees, assumptions, acceptance and change control, with examples of what goes wrong when they are missing.
- [What to include in an NDA: a clause-by-clause checklist](https://bodyatlas.github.io/clausery/guides/what-to-include-in-an-nda.html): The clauses a non-disclosure agreement needs, from the definition of confidential information to exclusions, term, return of information and governing law, and when to use a mutual or one-way NDA.

## Free tools
- [Amount in words converter for contracts and cheques](https://bodyatlas.github.io/clausery/free-tools/amount-in-words.html): Write any amount in words for contracts, cheques and promissory notes, such as "One Thousand Two Hundred and Fifty Dollars and 50/100".
- [Contract deadline calculator (business days, months, years)](https://bodyatlas.github.io/clausery/free-tools/deadline-calculator.html): Add or subtract days, business days, weeks, months or years from a date, with month-end handling and your own holidays.
- [Word template tag checker](https://bodyatlas.github.io/clausery/free-tools/template-checker.html): Check a .docx template for broken {tags} and see the questionnaire it would produce. The file never leaves your computer.

## Comparisons
- [Gavel alternative that keeps client data on your computer](https://bodyatlas.github.io/clausery/compare/gavel-alternative.html): Gavel is a well-regarded cloud platform for legal document automation and client workflows. Clausery does the core job, turning Word templates into guided questionnaires, without sending client data to a vendor.
- [Clio Draft alternative for firms that cannot upload client files](https://bodyatlas.github.io/clausery/compare/clio-draft-alternative.html): Clio Draft (formerly Lawyaw) is document automation that lives inside the Clio ecosystem. Clausery is independent of any practice management system and never uploads the documents it builds.
- [HotDocs alternative: lightweight document automation in the browser](https://bodyatlas.github.io/clausery/compare/hotdocs-alternative.html): HotDocs has been a standard for enterprise document assembly for decades. Clausery is a much lighter tool: no installation, no server, and no component library to learn, for firms that need the essentials.
- [docassemble alternative that needs no server](https://bodyatlas.github.io/clausery/compare/docassemble-alternative.html): docassemble is a powerful, free, open-source platform for guided interviews, widely used in access-to-justice projects. It runs on a server you host. Clausery runs in the browser with nothing to install or host.
